corpus.title: White House Rejects UN Report Alleging US War Crimes In Iran
corpus.signal_text:
White House Rejects UN Report Alleging US War Crimes In Iran
The White House has rejected a report by a UN independent fact-finding mission that said there were reasonable grounds to believe the United States had committed war crimes during two air strikes in Iran.
The Independent International Fact-Finding Mission on Iran said in a report released on September 17 that there were reasonable grounds to believe US forces committed the war crime of launching indiscriminate attacks during strikes on a school in Minab and a sports facility in Lamerd on February 28.
The two strikes killed at least 178 civilians, including women and children, according to the mission. The Minab strike hit the Shajareh Tayyebeh Primary School and killed more than 150 people, including about 120 schoolchildren.
A separate strike on a sports complex and surrounding residential area in Lamerd killed 22 civilians.
In a scathing written response to the report, White House Deputy Press Secretary Anna Kelly rejected the findings, saying: "The only party in this conflict that has committed war crimes is the Iranian regime, which has murdered thousands of its own people, killed Americans overseas, executed acts of terrorism in the Strait of Hormuz, and launched indiscriminate attacks against its neighbors in the region."
Kelly also said the UN Human Rights Council had "accomplished nothing for human rights while spouting unserious nonsense for decades."
US officials have repeatedly said military operations are conducted in accordance with the law of armed conflict and that an investigation is ongoing.
The report is scheduled to be formally presented to the 47-member UN Human Rights Council in Geneva on September 21.
The mission also found reasonable grounds to believe that Iranian authorities committed crimes against humanity during their crackdown on nationwide protests in December-January. It cited unlawful killings, arbitrary detention, torture, and other inhumane acts committed as part of a widespread and systematic attack against civilians.
